subject.title: [Bug]: Cron agent jobs silently time out during sustained LLM API outages instead of fast-failing on definitive errors

question: For plain provider 500/API-error failures in isolated cron jobs, should OpenClaw treat them as cron-local transient timeout/server_error failures, shared provider-profile cooldown signals, or skipped provider-outage runs?
rationale: The source already contains partial retry and alert plumbing, but the remaining behavior changes provider routing, auth-profile health, skipped-vs-failed semantics, and user notification policy.

options.title: Cron-local outage handling
options.body: Classify the exact plain API 500 shape for cron/fallback retry and notification without poisoning shared auth-profile health, then prove the fallback chain finishes before the cron wall-clock timeout.

options.title: Shared provider cooldown
options.body: Let repeated provider 500s cool down or skip same-provider auth profiles globally, accepting the risk that a transient provider outage can suppress otherwise healthy sessions.

options.title: Fold into broader guardrails
options.body: Keep this issue blocked behind https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/14376 and solve it only as part of a reason-aware cron policy layer.

recommendation.title: Cron-local outage handling
recommendation.body: Classify the exact plain API 500 shape for cron/fallback retry and notification without poisoning shared auth-profile health, then prove the fallback chain finishes before the cron wall-clock timeout.

likelyOwner.reason: They carried the merged structured `server_error` cron retry work that defines the closest existing policy boundary.
